OCCIPUT–T3AUS

REFORM® POCT

Posterior Occipito-Cervico-Thoracic Fixation · Precision Spine

Modular posterior fixation, Occiput–T3

Polyaxial screws, occipital plates & screws, dual-diameter rods, cross-connectors, lateral offsets, dominoes and hooks combine to match patient anatomy. Ti, Ti-alloy or CoCr — do not mix with stainless steel.

Design Features

Y & A ShapeMidline fixation footprints
Contour ZonesBetter bone-plate interface

Total freedom. 10mm of tulip translation per size, ±30° tulip rotation, ±15° cephalad/caudal tulip angulation — minimises rod contouring across the occipito-cervical junction.

Available in Y-Shape and A-Shape orientations, each in Small/Medium/Large. Position centred in the midline, immediately below the inion, between the external occipital protuberance and the posterior border of the foramen magnum.

1

Preoperative Planning

Image the patient's osseous anatomy to plan hardware size and type. Position prone with the head and neck held securely in optimal alignment. Standard midline incision at the appropriate levels.

2

Polyaxial Screw Technique

Locate the entry point and trajectory; perforate the cortex with the Bone Awl (55-IN-0010) to prevent drill walk-off.

Use the Fixed Drill Guide (55-IN-0030) with 12/14/16mm Bone Drills (undersized 1mm), or the Adjustable Drill Guide (55-IN-0040) with a single Adjustable Drill Bit set to the desired depth on its sliding sleeve.

Verify pathway integrity with the Ball-tip Sounder and confirm depth with the Depth Gauge. Tap to length, then assemble the Polyaxial Screw to the Polyaxial Screw Driver and advance to depth. Orient the tulip with the Tulip Manipulator.

!

Note: the Adjustable Drill Bit should not be used with the Fixed Drill Guides.

3

Rod Placement

Seat the appropriately sized Stabilization Rod into each tulip with the Rod Holder. The Flexible Rod Template can guide contour; the Rod Cutter shortens rods; the Standard Rod Bender contours as needed. Lateral Offsets and Dominoes may be added to match anatomy.

4

Rod Reduction

Use the Rod Pusher, Rod Reduction Gun, Rod Tower Reducer and/or Rod Reduction Rocker to seat the rod. Insert a Cap Screw with the Single- or Dual-Sided Cap Screw inserter and hand-tighten at each screw.

5

Final Tightening

Assemble the Counter Torque Wrench to each Polyaxial Screw and drive the Torque Driver through the wrench barrel until the Modular Torque Handle's limit is reached.

27 in-lbs ± 10%
6

Hook Technique

Select hook size/orientation for anatomy; assemble to the Hook Holder and place under the superior or inferior lamina (cranial or caudal). Repeat Rod Placement → Final Tightening to finish the hook construct.

7

Cross-Connector Technique

Use the Cross-connector Calipers to size, then place with the Cross-connector Inserter. Rod-to-Rod: seat each hook end, rotate the Cross-connector & Domino Inserter 90° to engage the rod cam. Head-to-Head: insert the Head-to-Head Cap Screw through the tulip, torque with the Head-to-Head Counter Torque Wrench, then add the Head-to-Head Locking Cap.

27 in-lbs ± 10%
8

Occipital Plate Size & Positioning

Measure occipital bone thickness on x-ray to select screw length. Centre the plate in the midline immediately below the inion, optimising the relationship between the plate tulips and the cervical fixation point.

9

Plate Contouring

Contour with the Bending Iron Short + Long together at the plate's contour zones, or with the Occipital Plate Bender's anvil/wedge over the contour zone.

!

Care should be taken to not over-bend the plate in any direction.

10

Occipital Plate & Polyaxial Screw Technique

Place the plate with the All-in-One Plate Inserter and Guide, drill to depth (Angled Bone Drill optional), tap (Angled Tap optional), then drive the appropriate-length Occipital Screw (Angled Screw Driver optional). Remove the guide and repeat for remaining holes.

11

Occipital Rod, Reduction & Final Tightening

Seat the appropriately lordosed Pre-lordosed Occipital Rod (Flexible Rod Template optional; Rod Cutter to shorten). Reduce with the Rod Pusher / Rod Reduction Gun / Rod Tower Reducer / Rod Reduction Rocker, hand-tighten a Cap Screw at every tulip, then final-tighten with the Occipital Counter Torque Wrench.

27 in-lbs ± 10%
12

System Removal

Reverse the order of implant procedures.

Indications, contraindications & warnings (summary)
Indications — Immobilisation/stabilisation as an adjunct to fusion for acute/chronic instabilities of the craniocervical junction, cervical spine (C1–C7) and thoracic spine T1–T3: traumatic spinal fractures/dislocations; instability or deformity; failed previous fusion; tumours involving the cervical spine; degenerative disease with radiculopathy and/or myelopathy confirmed by imaging. Also for restoring spinal column integrity in advanced-stage cervical tumour patients pending fusion.

Contraindications — use below T3; osteopenia/bone absorption/joint or soft-tissue disease at the site; metal/coating intolerance; fever, elevated WBC or other active infection/inflammation; obesity; mental illness; pregnancy; any case needing mixed metals; patient unwilling/unable to follow post-op instructions.

Key warnings — single use only, never re-implant; do not mix Titanium with stainless steel components; components are supplied non-sterile and must be sterilised before use; components of this system must not be combined with another system or manufacturer's components; benefit of fusion with pedicle-type screw systems has not been established for stable spines; implantation should only be performed by surgeons experienced with pedicle screw spinal systems.

Refer to the current Precision Spine Instructions for Use (IFU) for the complete indications, contraindications, warnings and potential adverse effects — this app is a quick reference only.
